findings.title: XSS Filter Bypass - JS String Escape + Template Literal (CTF Flag)
findings.description:
The /page endpoint reflects the `name` parameter inside a JavaScript string: `var name = "VALUE"`. A WAF-like filter blocks: single quotes ('), uppercase letters (A-Z), and angle brackets (<). The server also escapes double-quote (") to (\")

Bypass chain:
1. Escape-the-escape: send backslash before the double-quote (\\"): server escapes " to \" but the preceding \\ becomes an escaped backslash in JS (\\\\), allowing the " to terminate the string
2. Template literal (backtick): use backtick instead of ' or " for the alert argument
3. Hex escape: use \\x58\\x53\\x53 instead of 'XSS' to avoid uppercase letters

Final payload: \\"%;alert(`\\x58\\x53\\x53`)//
URL: /page?name=%5C%22%3Balert%28%60%5Cx58%5Cx53%5Cx53%60%29%2F%2F
